query: For lightweight high-entropy alloys intended for weight-critical aerospace and rail-transport applications, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain their ability—or inability—to combine low density with mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance? Specify an unnamed controlled comparison that would test the hypothesis, the observations predicted relative to a baseline alloy, the conditions under which the hypothesis should cease to hold, the existing observations that support it, and a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In equimolar Ti–V–Cr–Mn–Co lightweight high‐entropy alloys, adding ~7 at.% Al induces the formation of nanoscale L12‐ordered Al-rich precipitates that both obstruct dislocation motion (raising room‐temperature strength) and serve as an Al reservoir to grow a continuous protective Al2O3 scale during high‐temperature oxidation, thereby enabling the simultaneous achievement of low density, high mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and high‐temperature oxidation resistance.
generation.material_initial_state: Equimolar Ti–V–Cr–Mn–Co high‐entropy alloy without Al
generation.intervention: Addition of 7 at.% Al replacing equal fractions of Ti, V, Cr, Mn, and Co
generation.conditions: Room‐temperature tensile testing; 100 h oxidation in air at 800 °C; corrosion testing in 3.5 wt.% NaCl at room temperature
generation.structural_mediator: Nanoscale L12-ordered Al-rich precipitates within the matrix
generation.mechanism: These precipitates impede dislocation glide (increasing yield strength) and provide a concentrated Al source at the surface for rapid formation of a continuous Al2O3 scale under high‐temperature exposure
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the Al‐free baseline, the Al‐containing alloy will show ≥20% higher yield strength, ≥50% lower oxidation mass gain after 100 h at 800 °C, and equal or higher pitting potential in 3.5 wt.% NaCl
generation.baseline: Equimolar TiVCrMnCo HEA without Al: yield strength ≈750 MPa; oxidation mass gain ≈2 mg/cm2 after 100 h at 800 °C; pitting potential ≈–0.2 V vs. SCE in NaCl
generation.boundary: At temperatures ≥900 °C or Al contents >10 at.% the L12 precipitates coarsen or transform, and the combined strength/oxidation‐resistance benefit diminishes
generation.uncertainty: The precise Al threshold for stable L12 precipitate formation and the coarsening kinetics at intermediate temperatures are not fully quantified

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize two alloys: (1) equimolar TiVCrMnCo, (2) TiVCrMnCo with 7 at.% Al. Use TEM and XRD to detect L12 precipitates. Perform room‐temperature tensile tests, 100 h oxidation at 800 °C in air, and corrosion tests in 3.5 wt.% NaCl.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Al‐containing alloy shows no L12 precipitates or improves neither yield strength by ≥10% nor reduces oxidation mass gain by ≥10% relative to the baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
